text:
dana: Heads-up — ACME legal pushed back on the exec signoff. They require a written data classification mapping and a confirmation that customer keys never leave their VPC. They used the phrase 'no external KMS' on the call. Need options and ETA. cc @li @rachel
li: Can you paste the exact ask from legal? Is this for the POC only or a contract term?
dana: POC -> exec signoff for enterprise contract. Exact wording: 'keys must be customer-managed and not be exported or stored outside our network; we need attestations and a vendor crypto addendum.'
omar: Short summary: our Private deployment supports BYO-KMS and customer-managed key endpoints, but integration with ACME's vendor HSM will need an engineering integration (key exchange + attestation). Estimate: 3-5 dev days + security review. Unknowns: vendor API, attestation style, TLS peering details.
rachel: Security note: we can support BYO-KMS if customer accepts an attestation flow and we get vendor crypto docs + key lifecycle policy. We'll also need audit log delivery and a signed SOC2 Addendum. I'll list the exact docs we need.
cameron: Pricing note: Private + BYO-KMS integration = one-time integration fee + platform premium. Ballpark: $35k setup + $12k/mo for dedicated capacity at scale. Need final capacity numbers to firm it up.
dana: They also asked for a 200 qps throughput SLA across 8 regions for inference. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
omar: 200 qps geo-distributed is non-trivial. Options: 1) replicate capacity per region (expensive) 2) geo-fanout with regional replicas + caching 3) staged rollout (start with 3 regions). I'll need eng-infra numbers to convert to GPUs.
eng-infra-bot: eng-infra: preliminary calc: to hit ~200 qps steady across 8 regions we'd expect ~12-16 A100-equivalent devices (depends on model & quant). For POC we recommend starting in 3 regions and using burst capacity and smart routing.
li: Short-term workaround suggestion: while BYO-KMS is integrated, offer a tightly-scoped hosted POC with ephemeral keys + strict routing and auditable key access, if legal signs a timeboxed risk acceptance. That buys time for the integration.
rachel: That workaround requires an explicit risk acceptance signed by ACME CISO and a list of required audit logs. We also need to vet the ephemeral key exchange for compliance.
dana: Action items & owners (deadline: EOD):
- Omar: integration scope + dev ETA (owner: omar)
- Eng-infra: capacity & GPU estimate by region (owner: eng-infra)
- Cameron: detailed pricing/quote + setup fee (owner: cameron)
- Rachel: security checklist & doc request for ACME legal (owner: rachel)
Please ack. I'll schedule a 4pm exec bridge if we have numbers.
omar: Ack — I'll scope and post a short estimate by 14:00.
eng-infra-bot: Ack — posting region-level counts and cost by 16:00.
cameron: Ack — will draft quote and run thru pricing-ops, sending a preliminary PDF by 17:00.
rachel: Ack — sending questionnaire + required vendor doc list to dana for outreach.
dana: If anyone hits a blocker that pushes these past EOD, ping me immediately. I want exec coverage on the 4pm call.
li: Example config snippet for customer-managed endpoint we discussed: 
```
vault:
  backend: kms
  provider: customer
  endpoints:
    - https://kms.acme.example
  attestation: true
```
li: Also adding: @cameron can we include a temporary credit for the POC if they sign the risk acceptance for the hosted workaround?
cameron: We can offer a one-month credit for the hosted trial, but only if legal signs the risk acceptance and we get CISO confirmation.
dana: Good. Final: I'll compile notes into the exec-bridge doc and invite ACME CISO + our CTO if we have concrete numbers. Everyone, please drop updates into this thread — short replies only so I can forward to the execs.
escalation-bot: :warning: Escalation reminder — this thread flagged HIGH-PRIORITY. If there is no response from owners within 24h, deal will be re-triaged.
dana: Thanks all.
